manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Stand the gum bottle upright on the red card.

Task description: Pick up the green-and-white gum bottle currently lying on the table and place it upright on the red card.

Success criteria: The gum bottle is picked up and set down with its base inside and touching the red card, standing upright and remaining stable on its own after release.

## Execution tips

- Grip both sides around the middle of the bottle’s straight cylindrical section, avoiding the cap edge and curved ends. Let the pads contact fully and leave room to place the bottle bottom.
- When approaching a horizontal bottle, close perpendicular to its long axis and open slightly wider than the grasp section. Before closing, use both views to confirm the fingers are on opposite sides, avoiding pushing from one side and rolling it away.
- After grasping, make a small test lift to see whether the bottle body slides. When turning it upright, adjust where both ends have room to rotate clear of the table, avoiding contact between either end and the tabletop.
- During placement, let the bottle base lie flat on the card and rest on the table before releasing gradually. Open the gripper until there is clearance from the bottle, then withdraw to avoid tipping the bottle or moving the card.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start exactly one real-robot episode with your specified parameters and follow the returned manual and live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode and report my observation-based assessment and the recording directory.

I have read the returned manual. Live images show the bottle lying left of the red card. I am adjusting the right-arm approach angle to align with the body middle, then will test the grasp with a small lift.

Feedback is normal during approach, and the bottle has not been touched. Next I will use smaller steps and both views to confirm the pads are on opposite sides of the body; after lifting, I will check the available space for turning it over.

The gripper is near the bottle body and is descending in steps no greater than 1 cm. The bottle remains in place; before closing, I still need to confirm the finger pads are at the right contact height.

The image did not confirm that the bottle left the table after a small test lift; the grasp is still unreliable. I opened the gripper and will lower the contact height before regrasping, continuing within this episode.

The bottle has now left the table with the gripper, whose actual opening remains approximately 52 mm. The bottle has rotated slightly downward. I will first check grasp stability, then adjust orientation in stages within joint clearance.

I observed that the grasp point is too close to the bottle bottom, causing the body to rotate during lifting. I have lowered the bottle back to the table; next I will move the grasp point toward the middle of its body to reduce slipping while turning it.

After adjusting the grasp position, the bottle is again off the table, and the grip is more stable than last time. I am increasing clearance from the table, then will turn it toward the red card in stages and bring it upright.
The bottle is above the area to the left of the red card, cap up and bottom down. Next I will align its bottom inside the card area and lower in small steps to check that the table supports it.
The bottle base is aligned inside the card and appears close to its surface. I am using smaller lowering steps to confirm contact, then will release gradually and check whether it stands on its own.

After release, the bottle remained upright with its bottom inside the red card. The gripper is open and retreating. I will check once more that it neither drags nor topples the bottle before ending the episode.
